guideTitle: Best Wet Tile Saws for Bathrooms and Floors (2026)
metaTitle: Best Wet Tile Saws for DIY
metaDescription: Compare six wet tile saws by blade size, motor, rip and diagonal capacity, bevel range, stand and water system, for bathroom, kitchen and floor tile jobs.
expertTake: The DEWALT D36000S is the top pick because it states a 15 amp motor, 37 inch rip capacity and a cutline indicator with stainless rollers that hold accuracy to 1/32 inch over 30 inches. The EliteEdge 7 inch is the value pick for a small bathroom job. Skip the category if you tile a single backsplash, because a manual snap cutter and a rental saw for the odd cut cost far less than buying one.
introParagraphs: A wet tile saw is a diamond-bladed saw with a water reservoir that cools the blade and holds down dust as it cuts ceramic, porcelain and stone tile. A sliding tray or rolling table pushes the tile past the blade, which gives straight, clean cuts that a hand cutter cannot match on hard materials.

Blade size, motor power, cutting capacity, table travel and the water system decide what you can cut and how well. This guide compares saws for home tile jobs, from compact benchtop models to large stand-mounted machines.

products.name: DEWALT D36000S 10 in 15-Amp Wet Tile Saw with Stand
products.description:
The DEWALT D36000S is a 10 inch wet tile saw with a 15 amp motor rated at 1,220 watts maximum watts out, a stand, a 37 inch rip capacity (41 inches with a plunge cut) and an 8-1/2 inch crosscut capacity. The listing says a cutline indicator, a rigid frame and stainless steel rollers keep cutting accuracy to within 1/32 inch over 30 inch cuts, and that it can rip 36 by 36 inch tiles.

The tradeoff is price and weight. It is the most expensive of the eight candidates, and a 10 inch saw with a stand takes real space and is awkward to move. Compared with the DEWALT D24000S, it adds rip capacity and a stronger motor. Compared with the 7 inch benchtop saws, it handles large format tiles that they cannot.

In ownership, change the water often, clean the tray and rollers after each job and use a diamond blade suited to porcelain. A wet saw is messy, so work outside or on a protected surface. Wear eye and ear protection.
products.bestFor: Remodelers and serious DIYers who cut large-format porcelain and many tiles.
pros: Stated 37 inch rip capacity and 18 inch clearance handle 36 by 36 inch tiles
15 amp motor cuts dense porcelain without bogging down
Cutline indicator and stainless rollers hold accuracy to 1/32 inch over 30 inches
Includes a stand, which saves buying one separately
cons: Most expensive of the eight candidates in this comparison
Large size and weight make it a poor fit for tight spaces or a single small job

products.name: DEWALT D24000S 10 in Wet Tile Saw with Stand, 1.5 HP Peak
products.description:
The DEWALT D24000S is a 10 inch wet tile saw with a stand, a 1.5 HP peak motor, an 18 by 18 inch diagonal cut capacity and a maximum depth of cut of 3-1/8 inches. It weighs 69 lb, and the listing includes a 10 inch XP4 porcelain blade.

The tradeoff is capacity. Compared with the D36000S, it handles smaller tiles and has less rip length, though it costs less, seventh of eight. Compared with the Hoteche 8 inch, it has a bigger blade and a stand but costs more.

In ownership, the weight makes it stable but awkward to move. Fill the reservoir to the right level, keep the blade pointed in the right direction and clean the tray after use. A good diamond blade matters more than the saw for chipping, so check the blade type for porcelain.
products.bestFor: Homeowners who tile a few rooms and want a proven, stable 10 inch saw.
pros: Stated 18 by 18 inch diagonal capacity handles most common floor tile sizes
Max depth of cut of 3-1/8 inches also cuts thick stone and pavers
Included XP4 porcelain blade and stand mean it works out of the box
Seventh of eight in price, below the D36000S
cons: Seventh of eight in price, which is still high for a single project
Less rip capacity than the D36000S, so large-format tiles are tight

products.name: Hoteche 8 in Benchtop Wet Tile Saw with Stand, 8 Amp
products.description:
The Hoteche is an 8 inch benchtop wet tile saw with an 8 amp motor, a no-load speed of 3550 RPM, a saw body that tilts between 45 and 90 degrees for bevel cuts and a durable stand. The listing says the spacious table helps support the tile.

The tradeoff is brand backing and capacity. An 8 amp motor is less powerful than the DEWALT, and the listing in our data gives no rip or depth capacity. Compared with the 7 inch saws, it has a larger blade for thicker tile. Compared with the DEWALT D24000S, it is cheaper at sixth of eight and lighter.

In ownership, a tilting body is useful for bevel and mitered edges. Keep the water level correct, check blade alignment and clean the tray after each job. Choose a blade rated for porcelain if you will cut it.
products.bestFor: DIYers who cut mid-size tile and want a stand and a tilting body.
pros: Eight inch blade handles thicker tile than the 7 inch saws
Tilting saw body allows bevel cuts from 45 to 90 degrees
Stand included for a stable working height
Sixth of eight in price, well below the DEWALT saws
cons: Listing in our data gives no rip or depth capacity figures
8 amp motor is less powerful than the DEWALT motors on dense porcelain

products.name: FLEX CS 40 Wet Tile Saw, 12,000 RPM, 5 in Blade

specList.label: Blade
specList.value: 5 inch with 7/8 inch arbor, 20 mm adapter ring

products.description:
The FLEX CS 40 is a compact wet tile saw with a 5 inch blade on a 7/8 inch arbor with a 20 mm adapter ring, a no-load speed of 12,000 RPM and a tilting range of 0 to 45 degrees. It is sold as a small, portable cutter.

The tradeoff is capacity. A 5 inch blade cuts only a shallow depth, so it will not cut thick stone or large tiles in one pass. Compared with the Hoteche 8 inch, it is smaller and easier to carry. Compared with the DEWALT 10 inch, it is for small jobs and thin tile.

In ownership, a small saw is easy to store and carry to a site. Keep the blade wet, use the right blade for porcelain and clean the tray. It suits trim work, mosaic and small tile repairs, but not a large floor.
products.bestFor: Small repairs, mosaic and backsplash jobs where portability matters.
pros: Compact 5 inch size is easy to carry and store
Tilts 0 to 45 degrees for bevel cuts on small tiles
Includes a 20 mm adapter ring for different arbors
Fifth of eight in price, in the middle of the group
cons: 5 inch blade has a shallow maximum cutting depth
Not suited to large-format tiles or thick stone

products.name: VEVOR 7 in Wet Tile Saw with 65Mn Blade, 3600 RPM, 0 to 45 Tilt
products.description:
The VEVOR 7 inch saw uses a 65Mn steel blade at 3600 RPM, with a 0 to 45 degree adjustable cutting angle, a maximum depth of 1.2 inches (30 mm) and a detachable polypropylene water reservoir that keeps the work area wet.

The tradeoff is that a 65Mn steel blade is a general blade and a diamond blade is better for porcelain, and a 1.2 inch depth limits thick tile. Compared with the EliteEdge, it is similar in size and slightly more expensive, fourth of eight. Compared with the Hoteche 8 inch, it is smaller and has no stand listed.

In ownership, check the blade type and consider a diamond blade for hard tile. Fill the reservoir, keep the tray clean and use the bevel on test pieces first. It suits bathroom wall tile and small floors.
products.bestFor: Bathroom wall tile and small floors where cost matters.
pros: Seven inch blade is a good size for wall and small floor tile
Adjustable 0 to 45 degree cut supports miters and trim pieces
Detachable water reservoir makes cleaning and refilling simpler
Fourth of eight in price, below the 8 and 10 inch saws
cons: Stated 1.2 inch maximum depth limits thick tile and stone
A 65Mn steel blade is not ideal for porcelain, so a diamond blade is wise

products.name: EliteEdge 7 in Wet Tile Saw, 3450 RPM, Bevel 0 to 45 Degrees

specList.label: Water
specList.value: Reservoir to dampen dust and debris

products.description:
The EliteEdge 7 inch saw has a 3450 RPM no-load induction motor, a 0 to 45 degree bevel adjustment and a water reservoir that dampens dust and debris. It is the third cheapest of the eight candidates.

The tradeoff is brand and detail. The listing gives limited cutting depth and capacity figures in our data, and a smaller saw cuts only small tile. Compared with the VEVOR 7 inch, it is cheaper and describes an induction motor. Compared with the Hoteche, it has a smaller blade and no stand.

In ownership, an induction motor is quieter and lasts longer than a brushed one. Keep the reservoir full, use a diamond blade for hard tile and clean the tray after use. It is a sensible choice for a small bathroom project.
products.bestFor: Small bathroom and backsplash projects on a tight budget.
pros: Third of eight in price, one of the lowest-cost 7 inch saws
Induction motor runs quieter and longer than a brushed motor
Bevel from 0 to 45 degrees supports miters and trim cuts
Water reservoir dampens dust and cools the blade
cons: Limited cutting depth and capacity figures in the data we had
Seven inch blade cannot handle large-format or thick tile

buyingCriteria.explanation: Blade diameter decides maximum cutting depth and tile size. A 10 inch blade, as on the DEWALT saws, cuts up to 3-1/8 inches deep and handles large tiles. A 7 inch blade, as on the VEVOR and EliteEdge, cuts about 1.2 inches deep. A 5 inch blade, as on the FLEX, suits small cuts only.

Rip capacity is the longest straight cut, and the diagonal capacity is the largest square tile cut diagonally. The DEWALT D36000S lists a 37 inch rip, and the D24000S lists an 18 by 18 inch diagonal. Large-format tiles of 24 by 24 inches or more need the bigger capacity.

Dense porcelain needs a strong motor and a diamond blade. The DEWALT D36000S lists 15 amps, and the Hoteche 8 amps. A weak motor chips tile and burns blades. A good diamond blade matters more than the motor for clean edges.

Stainless rollers and a rigid frame, as on the DEWALT, keep cuts straight. Plastic tables flex and drift. A cutline indicator shows where the blade will cut. If you tile large rooms, accuracy over 30 inches matters, and cheaper saws can wander.

A pump or reservoir cools the blade and holds down dust. A detachable reservoir, as on the VEVOR, is easy to clean. Wet saws spray slurry, so work outdoors or on a protected surface. Silica dust is a serious hazard in dry cutting, so wet cutting is the safer method.

A stand, as on the DEWALT and Hoteche, sets a comfortable working height. A 10 inch saw weighs 69 lb, which is stable but awkward to move. Benchtop 7 inch saws are lighter. Check your space and where you will store the saw.

howWeEvaluated.title: Blade and capacity
howWeEvaluated.description: We evaluated blade sizes and stated capacities from the published listings, from 5 to 10 inches. We did not cut tile with any saw.

howWeEvaluated.title: Motor and accuracy
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared motor ratings and table design. The DEWALT D36000S lists 15 amps and a cutline indicator with stainless rollers.

howWeEvaluated.title: Water system and stand
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at reservoirs, stands and weight. The VEVOR has a detachable reservoir, and the DEWALT and Hoteche include stands.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership and upkeep
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered blade cost, slurry cleanup and rust from owner feedback patterns. Diamond blades wear, and water systems need regular cleaning.

howWeEvaluated.title: Claims and value
howWeEvaluated.description: We treated capacity and accuracy claims as maker figures. We weighed price position against blade size, motor and included stand.

cards.label: 10 inch saws
cards.text: The DEWALT D24000S and D36000S cut large tiles and thick stone with strong motors. They are heavy and cost more, but suit whole-room jobs.

cards.label: 7 inch saws
cards.text: The VEVOR and EliteEdge are light and cheap and cut standard bathroom tile. They limit depth and tile size.

howToChoose.note: Choose a 10 inch saw for floors and large tile, and a 7 inch saw for bathrooms and small jobs.

rows: Stable with a stand and large capacity
Stable 69 lb saw with a stand

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A blade size that suits your tile, a diamond blade rated for porcelain and a water reservoir you can refill easily. Work outdoors or on a protected surface, and wear eye and ear protection.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The DEWALT D36000S is the best for floors, and the EliteEdge and VEVOR are best for small bathroom jobs.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You tile whole floors, cut large-format porcelain or tile for a living, as with the DEWALT D36000S.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You have one bathroom to tile. The EliteEdge or VEVOR cover it, or you can rent a saw for the job.

maintenance.interval: Every few cuts or when cloudy
maintenance.why: Slurry clogs the pump and dulls the blade. Fresh water keeps the pump and the cut clean.
Dried slurry sets like cement and jams rollers. Rinse the tray and wipe the rails.
A dull blade chips tile and strains the motor. Use a diamond blade rated for your tile type.
Wet rails rust. A light oil coat keeps the sliding table smooth.
Pumps clog and hoses crack. Clear debris and replace worn parts before the next job.

faq.q: Why use a wet saw instead of a dry saw?
faq.a: Water cools the blade and holds down dust, which makes cleaner cuts and reduces silica dust. Dry cutting is dustier and harder on the blade.

faq.q: How much should I spend on a wet tile saw?
faq.a: Match it to the job. A 7 inch saw covers small bathroom jobs, and a 10 inch saw suits floors and large tile. A rental may beat buying for a single job.

faq.q: How long do wet saws last?
faq.a: Motors can last for years, while blades, pumps and rollers wear. No listing states a rated life, so clean after each job.
A continuous-rim diamond blade for ceramic and porcelain, and a segmented blade for stone. A cheap blade chips tile edges.

faq.q: Can I use a wet saw indoors?
faq.a: It is messy because it sprays slurry. Work outdoors or in a protected area, and use drop cloths and a sump for runoff.
A stand sets a comfortable working height and makes the saw stable. The DEWALT and Hoteche include one, and the small saws sit on a bench.
